title: TSMC Could Hit Its 2027 2nm Capacity Goals A Year Early As NVIDIA, AMD And Apple Pile On Orders For Latest Chipmaking Tech
source_used: Wccftech, relaying United Daily News (UDN), Commercial Times and a Bank of America estimate
key_facts: A report from Taiwan (UDN) says TSMC's 2-nanometre capacity could reach its 2027 goals a year early because of strong orders from Nvidia, AMD, Apple and Qualcomm.
UDN's latest estimate raises end-2026 2-nanometre capacity by as much as 20%, from around 100,000 to 120,000 wafers a month.
Earlier estimates put 2-nanometre capacity at 110,000 to 140,000 wafers a month by the end of 2027.
A Commercial Times report said TSMC has dedicated at least five fabs to 2-nanometre production.
Bank of America expects the 2-nanometre share of TSMC revenue to rise from 3% to 11% in the third quarter, ahead of TSMC's earnings.
BofA's chart shows utilisation of 5-nanometre-and-below capacity above 90% in Q3; it expects supply and consumption to pass 500,000 wafers a month by Q3 2028 with utilisation at 105%.
quote_evidence: The Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) is experiencing booming demand for its 2-nanometer chip manufacturing process technology, which has enabled it to meet 2027's production targets ahead of schedule, according to a report from Taiwan.

The UDN's report outlines that while TSMC's production capacity was previously estimated to sit at around 100,000 wafers per month at the high end by 2026 end, the latest estimate bumps it up by as much as 20% to 120,000 wafers per month.
Ahead of TSMC's earnings, BofA expects 2-nanometer's contribution to TSMC's revenue to jump from 3% to 11% in the third quarter.
why_it_matters_hint: Strong 2-nanometre demand from AI and phone chip designers could mean TSMC's newest process ramps faster than planned.
notes: All figures are media and analyst estimates, not TSMC figures. UDN original (Chinese) was not opened; credited as the first reporter named by Wccftech.
